newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Big Three banks up on privatisation scheme.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Big Three banks up on privatisation scheme.

text.p: Shares of Taiwan's "Big Three" state-run banks jumped at mid-morning Friday on hopes linked to the banks' speedy privatisation, brokers said.
After 70 minutes, at 0210 GMT, Chang Hwa Bank surged T$6 or 5.08 percent to T$124, First Commercial Bank gained T$5 or 4.27 percent to T$122, and Hua Nan Bank surged T$4.5 or 3.86 percent to T$121.

"The release of the banks' shares will create selling pressure in the short term, but from a longer term's point of view, privatisation will boost their operation efficiency," said George Hou, a fund manager of Jardine Fleming.
Some analysts have estimated the future underwriting price of the Big Three banks would be T$130 each, leaving room for potential rises.
In April, the Taiwan provincial government said it would shorten the period of the long-delayed sale of equity in the Big Three banks to 14 months from 18 months.
The provincial government's privatisation panel decided to release 15.9 percent of First Commercial's shares, 7.5 percent of Hua Han's and 4.6 percent in Chang Hwa's.
The provincial assembly started to review the proposed privatisation plan on Thursday, raising hopes that the privatisation will take place soon.
